settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: ParametersInterceptor.enableDynamicMethodInvocation is NOT set here; DefaultActionMapper.allowDynamicMethodCalls defaults false, blocking method:/!method traversal
DefaultActionMapper.allowedActionNames = [a-zA-Z0-9._!/\\-]* and cleanupActionName strips disallowed chunks from URIs
ReflectionContextState.setDenyMethodExecution(true) and setCreatingNullObjects(true) are set around setParameters
isAcceptableValue / isExcluded reject values matching excluded patterns before setParameter
candidates.description: The repository is the 2.3.x line (struts2-parent 2.3.20-SNAPSHOT). Untrusted HTTP request parameters flow through ParametersInterceptor.setParameters -> newStack.setParameter(name, value) into OGNL evaluation. Protection is layered: (1) isAcceptableParameter -> acceptableName (length limit, excluded patterns, accepted patterns) plus optional action-side ParameterNameAware.acceptableParameterName; (2) isAcceptableValue rejects values matching excluded patterns; (3) OgnlValueStack/ReflectionContextState sets deny-method-execution and creating-null-objects during binding; (4) dynamic method invocation (method:/action:/!method) is gated behind allowDynamicMethodCalls (default false) and allowActionPrefix (default false). The effectiveness of (1)/(2) depends on the *configured* excludedPatterns/acceptedPatterns values (e.g., struts.excludedPatterns) which are not in Java source in this snapshot; a permissive or empty exclude set would widen OGNL exposure. This is a candidate for the known 2.3.x OGNL-binding weakness, but the decisive configuration could not be read here.
missing_evidence: Actual struts.excludedPatterns / struts.acceptedPatterns values (struts-default.xml, struts.properties, web.xml) were not located/read
A specific reachable action property or ParameterNameAware implementation allowing metacharacter names was not identified
No end-to-end runtime confirmation of OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled expression
preconditions: Deployed app runs the reviewed 2.3.x code
struts.excludedPatterns / acceptedPatterns configured permissively or left in a state that does not block OGNL metacharacters like #, @, (, )
A reachable action with a settable property or a ParameterNameAware that returns true for metachar names
candidates.title: Struts2 version/branch is 2.3.x; OGNL parameter isolation depends on excluded-patterns configuration not verifiable from reviewed Java-only source

counter_evidence: allowActionPrefix defaults false (line 123) and allowActionCrossNamespaceAccess defaults false (line 124); both must be explicitly enabled
cleanupActionName still filters the resulting name through allowedActionNames
namespace is used to look up actions in config, and action-name allowlisting remains in effect
candidates.description: DefaultActionMapper supports the 'action:' prefix which sets the mapping name from a request parameter key when allowActionPrefix is enabled, and optionally allows cross-namespace access when allowActionCrossNamespaceAccess is enabled. If an application enables cross-namespace access, a request-supplied parameter name can select an action name in a different namespace than intended, bypassing namespace-based authorization assumptions. The defaults here are false, so this is configuration-dependent rather than a source defect, but the code path is exposed and worth flagging as a candidate.
missing_evidence: Application struts.xml/struts.properties enabling these options was not located
No concrete namespace-isolation boundary in a consuming app was analyzed
preconditions: Security model relies on namespace separation
candidates.title: Open (cross-namespace) action mapping can be enabled via struts.mapper.action.prefix.enabled / crossnamespaces configuration
